searchNote: Searched October 27, 2026, twice. First on Zillow: every house listed for sale within about 13 miles of the daycare, asking $335,000 or less, with 3 or more bedrooms and 1,600 or more square feet. 61 matched, 31 of them new-construction floor plans with no history to report, so they are left out. That pass kept the existing houses with 4 or more bedrooms and a drive under 20 minutes, plus 17 Savoy Dr, a 3-bedroom in the same Lake Saint Louis association as Cadillac Ct. Then the same evening against the MLS feed, read through Realtor.com and Redfin, for all of St. Charles County under the same filters: 139 listings, 92 of them existing single-family houses. Every one was routed to the daycare, and the ones under 20 minutes were read for the two must-haves. That added six houses, all 3-bedroom ranches or splits the Zillow pass had skipped by asking for 4 bedrooms. Left out on purpose: 2451 Fox Bridge Ct, an attached villa with a $358 monthly association fee; 6 Westwood Estates Dr, a 24-minute drive; 500 Flowering Magnolia Dr, an attached villa with a $230 monthly fee and its bedrooms upstairs; 8 Roland Ln, with only 2 bedrooms on the main floor; and 37 Royal Oaks Dr, added from the feed and taken off the same evening when Google Maps put it at 22 minutes for noon on a Tuesday (typically 18 to 30). The company name says rentals, but no rental listing for the house turned up, so whether it was rented between 2024 and 2026 is unconfirmed.

sections.h: What has been done to it
ul: Roof replaced in 2024, according to the listing. Ask for the invoice and any warranty, since a roofer's warranty may transfer to a buyer.
The kitchen has white cabinets, a black microwave and a stainless range (listing photos 9 and 10). They look newer than 1978 but not recent.
Wood floors in the kitchen and dining room look refinished (photos 2, 3 and 8).
Siding is 80 percent vinyl and 20 percent stone, per the county, so the original 1978 siding has been covered or replaced.
The lower deck boards look newer than the upper deck (photos 25 to 27).
No building permits for the house turned up in a public search. Ask the seller for permits on the roof, the basement finish and any wall that was moved.

The headline price per square foot is misleading. At $289,999 it works out to $111 a square foot on all 2,608 finished square feet, against about $170 for recent Lake Saint Louis sales (Resideline, six months to late August 2026). Count only the 1,380 square feet above ground and it is $210 a square foot. Appraisers and buyers value basement space well below main-floor space.
Three of the four bedrooms are in the basement. The county record counts one bedroom above ground, so a family with small children sleeps on two different floors.
The interior needs flooring, paint and ceiling work throughout, and the seller will not do any of it (sold as-is).
The seller is an investor who paid $180,000 in April 2024. Even at $289,999 the investor clears roughly $110,000 before the roof, holding costs and commission, so there is room in the price.
A contract already failed once, which makes later buyers nervous, and the price was cut afterwards.

problems.title: Stained, worn carpet nearly everywhere
problems.body: Dark stains and traffic wear run through the living room (photos 4 to 7), the blue main bedroom (photo 11) and the whole lower level (photos 14 to 16). Spot patterns like these are often pets. Plan on pulling all of it and checking the subfloor and the concrete underneath for odor or moisture.
problems.cost: Estimated $7,000 to $14,000 for about 1,700 square feet, from typical St. Louis installed prices of $4 to $8 a square foot for carpet or vinyl plank.

problems.title: Unfinished drywall patch in the main bedroom
problems.body: A large section of the blue wall is patched and left unpainted (photo 11). Ask what was behind it: a leak, a hole or a moved outlet. A patch this size near windows can be a past water problem.
problems.cost: A few hundred dollars to finish, unless it hides water damage.

problems.title: Plywood patch under the upper deck
problems.body: The underside of the upper deck, right against the house, has a plywood patch over the boards (photo 25). That is where the deck attaches to the house, the most common spot for hidden rot and leaks into the wall. Have the inspector check the deck ledger, its flashing and the posts on both tiers.
problems.cost: Unknown until inspected. Minor flashing work runs hundreds; a two-tier deck rebuild can pass $20,000.

problems.title: Water management on a sloped, wooded lot
problems.body: Black corrugated drain pipes run from the downspouts out into the yard on both sides (photos 26 and 27), and the ground under the trees is bare dirt. Someone has been working to move water away from a walkout basement. Ask whether the basement has ever taken water, and look at the lower-level drywall and carpet edges for staining.
problems.cost: Grading or buried drain lines usually run $1,000 to $5,000 (estimate).

problems.title: Capped plumbing in the half bath
problems.body: The half bath has a capped pipe or valve on the wall beside the toilet (photo 17). A shower or tub may have been removed. If that half bath is the one in the basement, the three basement bedrooms have no shower on their floor.
problems.cost: Ask before pricing. Adding a shower back is roughly $5,000 to $12,000 (estimate).

problems.title: Textured popcorn ceilings throughout
problems.body: Every room in the photos has a sprayed texture ceiling. On a 1978 house that texture may contain asbestos. Test it before anyone scrapes it.
problems.cost: A lab test is about $50 to $100 a sample. Removal runs about $1 to $2 a square foot if it is clean and $3 to $7 if it needs abatement (estimates).

problems.title: Unknown furnace, air conditioner and water heater
problems.body: The listing names forced-air heat and central air with no ages. An investor listing that brags about a 2024 roof but stays quiet on the mechanicals usually means they are old. Ask for photos of the data plates.
problems.cost: Furnace and air conditioner together run $8,000 to $14,000; a water heater runs $1,500 to $2,500 (estimates).

problems.title: Electrical panel listed as Other
problems.body: The listing gives the electric service as Other. Houses from the 1970s sometimes carry Federal Pacific or Zinsco panels, which insurers dislike. Ask for a photo of the panel label.
problems.cost: A panel swap runs about $2,000 to $4,000 if needed (estimate).

problems.title: Big trees close to the house
problems.body: Mature oaks stand over the roof and around the back (photos 1, 26 and 27). Expect gutter clogging, limbs over the new roof, and roots near the sewer line. Get the sewer line camera-scoped.
problems.cost: A sewer scope is about $150 to $300. Tree trimming over the roof is often $500 to $2,000 (estimates).

problems.title: Radon in the basement bedrooms
problems.body: St. Charles County sits in the federal moderate radon category, and three bedrooms are below ground. Test before closing.
problems.cost: A test is $15 to $150. A mitigation fan system usually runs $1,000 to $1,500 if the reading is high (estimate).

problems.title: Taxes will likely rise
problems.body: The county raised the assessed value 26.8 percent in 2023 and 7.7 percent in 2025. Missouri reassesses in odd years, and a sale near $290,000 sits well above the county's current value of $246,930.
problems.cost: $3,301 for 2025. Expect more after the 2027 reassessment.
